title.narrative: EU Cyber Direct ¿ European Cyber Diplomacy Initiative

description.narrative: This Action aims to promote principles of the EU approach to cyberspace as defined in the 2015 Council Conclusions on Cyber Diplomacy, 2017 Joint Communication on Resilience, Deterrence and Defence and 2018 Council Conclusions on EU External Cyber Capacity Building Guidelines with a specific focus on promoting and protecting a global, open, free, stable and secure cyberspace where human rights and fundamental freedoms and the rule of law fully apply for the social well-being, economic growth, prosperity and integrity of our free and democratic societies. The project focuses on enhancing cyber security cooperation globally and strengthening the EU's role as a global security stakeholder, as foreseen in the EU's Global Strategy on Foreign and Security Policy.

comment.narrative: Governments of target countries vary in their approach to responsible state behaviour in cyberspace. While some of them belong to a group of likeminded countries e.g. US Japan South Korea others openly question the EU approach China or do not take any fixed position India Brazil.As a proxy we will use the way countries vote at the UN on two specific types of resolutions concerningICT in the context of international security Russia sponsored 143 voting yes abstaining or nonvoting Ref. year 2020Use of ICT for criminal purposes Russia sponsored 133 voting yes abstaining or nonvoting Ref. year 2019The baseline represents the starting point of the project.

Governments adopt positions on a single open free and secure cyberspace which fully reflects and respects core EU values of democracy human rights and the rule of law.The target represents a change in the two resolutions used as the proxy ICT in the context of international security or similar Maintaining or reducing the number of yes votes below 92 Ref. year 2024Use of ICT for criminal purposes or similar Maintaining or reducing the number of yes votes below 79 Ref. year 2024.

title.narrative: Outcome 1: To contribute to increased convergence of partner countries, regions and international organisations with EU positions on the application of existing international law in cyberspace, development of cyber norms and confidence building measures as well as digital standards, policies and good practices.

title.narrative: Number of processes related to the positions partner countries take in the runup to or during regional/international fora which have been influenced

description.narrative: Number of processes related to the positions partner countries take in the runup to or during regional/international fora which have been influenced

comment.narrative: Some target countries belong to a group of likeminded countries US Japan South Korea. Others openly question the EU approach. Many countries are still working on their positions with regards to the norms and the application of international law in cyberspace. While the baseline reflects the number of processes influenced by the EU Cyber Diplomacy Initiative at least 2 processes have previously been influenced during the EU Cyber Direct project.

The Action will aim to influence 10 processes at global and regional levels in line with EU values and priorities. These are for exampleGlobal processes UN First Committee UN Third Committee The Paris Call. Regional processes Promotion of the Council of Europe Budapest Convention and frameworks for responsible state behaviour and resilience in regional organisations such as NATO OECD OAS AUC ARF G20 and IBSA.
